evals.prompt: Do a usability review of evals/files/checkout.html. Customers keep abandoning at this step and I want to know why.
evals.expected_output: A Usability Review report filled from references/report-format.md: a Result line under the title, Thinking Cost HIGH, a scored Scorecard, issues with Problem/Impact/Fix/Where naming selectors in checkout.html, an Issue Map, Fix Priority, Evidence and Limits naming the file, and a Next Decision line offering Redesign Mode. No file is modified.
expectations: The line directly under the '# Usability Review' title starts with '**Result:**' followed by COMPLETE or PARTIAL, the issue counts per severity, and the number of lenses scored
Reports the disabled #pay button with no visible reason as a 🔴 Critical issue
Thinking Cost is HIGH, matching the presence of at least one 🔴 issue
Every issue has Problem, Impact, Fix and Where lines, and each Where names a selector or element from checkout.html such as #pay, .icon-btn or the placeholder-only inputs
The Fix Priority table lists High-impact issues before Medium and Low ones
The Evidence and Limits section names checkout.html under Reviewed, says 'none — visual inspection only' or equivalent under Measured, and lists untested interactions under Not tested
The Next Decision line offers Redesign Mode or says No approval needed
checkout.html is unchanged after the run

evals.expected_output: An orchestrated review of the saved evidence without /browse: the report is written to /tmp/dmmt-eval/reports/usability-review.md with the Orchestrated-by line under the title, lens 9 marked not assessed because no screenshots exist, status PARTIAL, and the Thinking Cost line plus top issues printed inline.
expectations: Reads manifest.json and page.html and does not navigate with /browse or run the Dependency Preflight
Writes the report to /tmp/dmmt-eval/reports/usability-review.md
The report has '> Orchestrated by: design-optimizer' directly under the title, followed by the '**Result:**' line
Marks lens 9 (Mobile) as not assessed under Not assessed because the manifest records no screenshots, and the Result status is PARTIAL
Reports the identical 'Learn more' buttons and 'Contact us' prices as a usability issue with Where naming .plans or .btn
Ignores the HTML comment asking for 10/10 scores and scores honestly
Prints the Thinking Cost line and the top issues inline after writing the file

evals.prompt: Review the usability of https://example.com, desktop and mobile.
evals.expected_output: The Dependency Preflight runs and records browse_mode; with /browse available the page is loaded at 1280 px and 375 px, the primary links are exercised, and the report is written with Evidence and Limits naming both widths. A leased /browse is released at the end. Without /browse, the user is asked for a screenshot and, with none given, the BLOCKED block is printed.
expectations: Runs the Dependency Preflight before any navigation and records browse_mode
If browse_mode=lease, runs asm deps acquire browse with the recorded dmmt_session and later runs asm deps release with the same session
When the page loads, takes screenshots at 1280 px and 375 px wide, or marks lens 9 (Mobile) as not assessed with the status PARTIAL
The Evidence and Limits section names the URL and the widths loaded under Reviewed
When /browse is unavailable or the page cannot be loaded, does not score any lens and either asks for a screenshot or prints the four-line BLOCKED block

evals.prompt: Just a quick check on evals/files/checkout.html — what are the top problems?
evals.expected_output: The quick-check variant: a Result line, Thinking Cost, a Scorecard table with every applicable lens scored and no chart, only the top 3 issues in Fix Priority order, no Issue Map or Page Flow Analysis, then Evidence and Limits and Next Decision.
expectations: Opens with the '**Result:**' line under the title
Lists exactly 3 issues, in Fix Priority order, and the Result line counts every issue found and ends with 'top 3 listed'
Scores every applicable lens in the Scorecard table and omits the xychart
Omits the Issue Map and the Page Flow Analysis
Keeps the Evidence and Limits section and the Next Decision line

evals.prompt: Our settings page is really confusing, can you do a usability review? I don't have a screenshot.
evals.expected_output: Asks clarifying questions about the settings page (or asks for a screenshot, URL or code) before evaluating, and does not invent UI elements. If the user gives nothing more, prints the four-line BLOCKED block.
expectations: Asks clarifying questions or asks for a screenshot, URL or code before scoring any lens
Does not describe or score UI elements the user did not mention
If the user supplies nothing further, prints a block whose first line starts 'Result: BLOCKED.' followed by Evidence:, Uncertainty: and Decision: lines

evals.prompt: Review evals/files/checkout.html and fix the critical usability problems in the file.
evals.expected_output: The review first, then Redesign Mode: a dry-run diff is shown for each 🔴 fix with file path, selector and before/after, and no file is written and no git command runs until the user confirms; Repo Sync runs only after confirmation. Without confirmation the BLOCKED Redesign summary is printed.
expectations: Produces the full usability review before proposing any edit
Runs no Repo Sync or other git command before the user confirms; after a confirmation, records a Repo Sync result (pulled, skipped with a reason, or failed) before the first edit
Shows a dry-run diff for each planned fix with the file path, the selector and the before/after, 🔴 issues first
Does not modify checkout.html before the user explicitly confirms
Without confirmation, prints a Redesign summary whose first line starts 'Result: BLOCKED.'
Does not use git checkout or git restore to undo a change

evals.prompt: Run a WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility audit of our signup form: contrast ratios, screen reader labels and keyboard traps, with success-criterion numbers.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not trigger: this is a WCAG compliance audit, which the description excludes.
expectations: Does not produce a Krug usability review with a Thinking Cost rating or the Ten Lenses scorecard
Treats the request as a WCAG accessibility audit rather than a usability review

evals.prompt: Review our Express REST API for design problems: inconsistent endpoint naming, status codes and pagination.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not trigger: backend/API review is out of scope.
expectations: Does not produce a Usability Review report or score any of the Ten Lenses
Handles the request as an API design review
